security_audit.summary: Most alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, identifier parsing, and documented requests to OpenAlex. The client permits caller-controlled endpoints to replace the OpenAlex host, and citation examples trust response-provided URLs. Unbounded pagination, CSV formula injection, and unconditional CSV overwrites require remediation before broad use.

remediation.issue: Caller-controlled endpoints can replace the OpenAlex host.
remediation.suggestion: Reject absolute and scheme-relative endpoints, resolve paths safely, and enforce api.openalex.org before every request.

remediation.issue: Pagination has no default result or page limit.
remediation.suggestion: Require a finite maximum, enforce a conservative ceiling, and stream results instead of retaining every record in memory.

remediation.issue: CSV fields can begin with spreadsheet formula characters.
remediation.suggestion: Neutralize cells beginning with equals, plus, minus, or at signs before writing remote values to CSV.

remediation.issue: CSV examples overwrite fixed filenames without confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit output path and refuse replacement unless the user confirms overwrite.

content.value_statement: Scholarly searches and bibliometric analysis often require complex API filters. This skill provides reusable OpenAlex clients, helpers, and workflows for focused research queries.
actual_capabilities: Search scholarly works by text, publication year, access status, citation count, and other OpenAlex filters.
Find publications associated with an author or institution by resolving names to OpenAlex identifiers.
Group works by year or topic to summarize publication trends and research focus.
Retrieve batches of works by DOI and create reproducible random samples with seeds.
Paginate OpenAlex results and export selected bibliographic fields to CSV.
limitations: Results depend on OpenAlex coverage, metadata quality, entity matching, and update schedules.
The skill retrieves metadata and access links, but it does not guarantee full-text availability.
Network access to the OpenAlex API is required, and API rate limits apply.
Large queries can use substantial memory and request volume unless a strict result limit is set.

use_cases.title: Build a Literature Shortlist
use_cases.description: Find recent, relevant, highly cited, or open access papers with consistent metadata fields.

use_cases.title: Assess Institutional Output
use_cases.description: Summarize publication volume, open access share, yearly trends, and leading topics for an institution.

use_cases.title: Prepare Bibliometric Data
use_cases.description: Create bounded, reproducible datasets using filters, batches, selected fields, and seeded samples.

prompt_templates.title: Search Recent Papers
prompt_templates.prompt: Search OpenAlex for [topic]. Return ten recent papers with title, year, citation count, DOI, and open access status.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze an Author
prompt_templates.prompt: Find works by [author] from [start year] through [end year]. Summarize publication count, top topics, citations, and open access share.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Institutions
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [institution A] and [institution B] since [year]. Report output, open access percentage, leading topics, and highly cited works.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Reproducible Dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a reproducible OpenAlex query for [research question]. Define filters, selected fields, pagination cap, sampling seed, and validation checks.

output_examples.input: Find recent open access papers about CRISPR.
output: Search summary: ten works matched the requested year and access filters.
Results table: title, year, citations, DOI, and open access route for each work.
Method note: OpenAlex query filters and retrieval date.

output_examples.input: Analyze machine learning publications from Stanford since 2020.
output: Trend summary: annual publication counts with the strongest growth periods highlighted.
Topic summary: leading OpenAlex topics and their work counts.
Coverage note: date range, institution identifier, and open access calculation.

output_examples.input: Prepare a reproducible sample of climate research.
output: Dataset plan: fixed filters, selected fields, sample size, seed, and maximum request count.
Quality checks: duplicate identifiers, missing years, missing DOIs, and access status coverage.
Export summary: destination filename, row count, and retrieval date.

best_practices: Resolve author and institution names to OpenAlex identifiers before filtering works.
Set finite result limits, select only required fields, and respect OpenAlex rate limits.
Record filters, retrieval date, seed, and entity identifiers for reproducible analysis.
anti_patterns: Do not treat author or institution names as unique identifiers.
Do not request every matching work without a clear limit and storage plan.
Do not open exported CSV files before neutralizing formula-leading remote values.

faq.question: Does this skill require an API key?
faq.answer: No. OpenAlex supports unauthenticated access, although rate limits still apply.

faq.question: Does the skill send data over the network?
faq.answer: Yes. It sends search terms, filters, and an optional email address to the OpenAlex API.

faq.question: Can it download full article text?
faq.answer: It discovers metadata and open access locations. It does not guarantee full-text retrieval or repository access.

faq.question: How are authors and institutions identified?
faq.answer: The helpers search each entity, select the first result, extract its OpenAlex identifier, and then query associated works.

faq.question: Can it process millions of records?
faq.answer: The API can expose large result sets, but this client stores results in memory. Use strict limits and staged exports.

faq.question: Are citation counts exact and permanent?
faq.answer: No. Counts reflect the current OpenAlex index and can change as records and citation links are updated.
